::: {.lead}
The course is built backwards from a single question: **how do you build a spoken dialogue system that can listen while it speaks, be interrupted, and know when it is its turn to talk?**
:::

Working back from that endpoint, the 14 weeks split into three parts. Part I lays the foundations — signals, alignment, representation learning and discretization. Part II takes the modules apart one at a time — ASR, TTS, and the acoustic front end. Part III arrives at audio-native language models and full-duplex architectures. The material tracks the 2025–2026 technical landscape and carries the derivations through rather than gesturing at them.

## Three Threads Through the Course

Every week comes back to these three questions. They are the coordinate system of the course, and the line that ties the 14 weeks together when you look back from the end.

| Thread | Question |
|---|---|
| **Representation** | What does this layer operate on — waveform / spectrogram / continuous SSL feature / discrete token? And what decides the frame rate? |
| **Latency** | How much of the latency budget does this module spend? Is it algorithmic latency (lookahead) or compute latency? |
| **Supervision** | Where does this capability come from — labeled data / self-supervision / synthetic data / human preference (RLHF)? |

## How to Use This Site

- **Read week by week**: the sidebar (top-left menu on mobile) groups the weeks into Part I / II / III, one page each. Every page carries the framing, learning objectives, the concept walkthrough, the mathematical skeleton, common misconceptions, a 180-minute time budget, demo suggestions, and references.
- **[Slides](slides.qmd)**: English slides, served as reveal.js pages with the in-class audio embedded. Press `S` for the presenter view, which includes the Chinese speaker notes.
- **Full-text search**: the box at the top right covers the whole site — the fastest way to locate a specific paper or concept.
- **[Full outline, single page](weeks/all.qmd)**: all 14 weeks strung together, for printing or reading straight through. Not recommended on mobile.
- **[Materials and resources](resources.qmd)**: textbook chapter mapping, a per-week "if you read only one paper" table, and toolchain suggestions.
- **Citation reliability**: a reference tagged `[驗]` still needs verification; `[主題]` means only search keywords are given, not a citation. See [Syllabus](syllabus.qmd).
